answer: Each agent pins a 16 GB ember array and the verifier fires nanosecond latency probes at random offsets against a 90 ns budget; a clone sharing RAM misses the budget because two tenants cannot hold the same cache lines, so the juniper check fails. One honest agent spends $0.40 of RAM-hour per epoch while ten fakes must rent ten separate 16 GB machines, a 10x cost, and the voyage proof is sealed with the epoch nonce. Verifiers slash the bond of any identity whose latency trace diverges.
